source_review.notes: Checked current NASA Product Integration, Integration Plan, Technical Assessment, Product Verification, Product Validation, Interface Management, and Configuration Management guidance; the official NASA Goddard systems-review standard; the official GAO Technology Readiness Assessment Guide representation; and official ISO metadata for ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2023. NASA resources returned HTTP 200. GAO and ISO returned HTTP 403 to the command-line client, but their current official web representations had already been inspected through the web retrieval path. The chapter treats system-level institutional reviews as examples and scopes its reusable readiness method to a declared integration decision.

evidence: Reviewed steps, configurations, environments, criteria, mandatory/supplementary partitions, evidence objects, applicability/support relations, findings, decision time, risk acceptance, authority, and deviation records.
Confirmed the readiness conjunction preserves criterion truth separately from risk/deviation authorization and conditions all findings on scope, configuration, environment, and time.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The descriptive completion fraction is explicitly excluded from the authorization predicate.

evidence: Executed integration-readiness-record-check and reproduced eight criteria, seven mandatory, four valid met mandatory criteria, exact unmet/expired/missing/waiver sets, and the hold decision.
Recomputed Example 1 as 18/20 = 0.90 while confirming the two mandatory gaps remain decision-dominant.
Recomputed Answer 1 as 10/12 = 0.833333 or approximately 83.3% while preserving the waived and expired mandatory findings as unmet.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All displayed arithmetic agrees with independent recomputation. The percentages are management descriptions, not probabilities or readiness proofs.

evidence: Confirmed ordinary readiness requires every applicable mandatory finding met, accepted residual risk, and present authority for the exact step/configuration/environment/time.
Confirmed an authorized deviation leaves the underlying criterion finding unmet rather than changing evidence truth.
Confirmed evidence applicability requires article/configuration compatibility, condition coverage, adequate method, provenance, freshness, and no invalidating change.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The model is a bounded assurance structure and makes no claim that a passed gate guarantees execution success.

evidence: Challenged percentage roll-ups, stale or missing evidence, supplier/configuration mismatch, visually compatible but miswired interfaces, unrehearsed human authority, expired calibration/training, bounded test doubles, waivers treated as green, destructive data change, and post-gate facility changes.

Reviewed item, interface, configuration, procedure, facility, enabling-product, people, safety, security/privacy, measurement/data, logistics, anomaly, rollback, external-system, decision-authority, and lifecycle boundaries.
Reviewed all ten examples and five answers for criterion truth, evidence applicability, mandatory gaps, conditional authorization, safe-state controls, dissent, invalidation, and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Actual high-consequence readiness still requires the independent domain, safety, security, quality, regulatory, operational, clinical, and stakeholder authorities applicable to the exposure.

evidence: Traced scope, criterion derivation, mandatory visibility, item identity, interface precheck, configuration coherence, environment, people, hazards, evidence capability, anomaly, rollback, dissent, decision, and change-invalidation invariants through exposition, examples, exercises, and answers.
Confirmed technology maturity, product acceptance, integration readiness, test readiness, verification, validation, operational readiness, and regulatory acceptance remain distinct.
Confirmed execution reconfirmation is required and gate findings do not persist automatically across material change or expiry.
invariant_checking.notes: Readiness is consistently treated as a contextual evidence-supported authorization, not a permanent item attribute.

proof_review.notes: The chapter presents a readiness predicate and evidence relations but no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Reviewed ready, met, valid, fresh, compatible, accepted, verified, validated, qualified, representative, current, complete, safe, and authorized language for explicit scope and evidence basis.
artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-038/report.json records exact local execution evidence for the declared readiness-record checker.

Supplier, qualification, calibration, training, rehearsal, test-double, analytical, prior-test, operational, and external-system evidence is bounded by article/configuration, conditions, method, result, date, provenance, anomalies, and limitations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external review is claimed. A gate pass is never presented as certainty of successful integration or as verification, validation, operational, production, regulatory, or lifecycle proof.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked integration readiness, entry/exit criterion, objective evidence, validity/freshness, mandatory criterion, waiver/deviation, readiness gate/finding, conditional authorization, hold point, and readiness debt. Criterion truth, risk acceptance, and decision authority remain separate.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked a misleading 90% roll-up, supplier option/firmware mismatch, harness pinout discrepancy, pressure-procedure authority, expired calibration, emulator fidelity, executing-shift qualification, bounded telemetry deviation, destructive schema migration, facility security change, and medication-pump integration. Each case ties the decision to exact configuration, people, evidence, hazards, rollback, and invalidation.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from scoped criteria through products/interfaces/configuration, procedures/environment/people, safety/security/data, anomalies/recovery, evidence validity/freshness/inheritance, gate conduct, outcomes, deviations, readiness debt, execution reconfirmation, and change invalidation. Ten examples and five complete answers require arithmetic, evidence appraisal, risk reasoning, decision-record critique, and sociotechnical readiness design.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, practitioner, architecture, mechanical, electrical, thermal, fluid, software, data, control, safety, security, privacy, accessibility, human-factors, supplier, facilities, logistics, quality, operations, maintenance, integration, verification, validation, regulatory, clinical, or affected-stakeholder review is claimed.
